title: Multi armed bandit governance for clinical AI deployment: adaptive model selection under delayed feedback (version 3.0.0)
description: Simulation framework for adaptive selection among frozen, independently validated ICU mortality prediction models under delayed outcome feedback, explicit cost and safety weights, and fixed confidence action elimination, evaluated on MIMIC-IV v3.1 with a temporally external deployment stream. Version 2.0.0 was a complete re analysis that supersedes version 1.0.0; version 3.0.0 revises the analysis after independent technical review (calendar ordering of development and deployment stays guaranteed by construction, arm C tuned by the common protocol, exact implied sample sizes, alert burden and cost vector sensitivity analyses, acquisition conditional costing, drift scenarios, a Gaussian posterior Thompson sampling variant, signed and patient experienced disparities, race subgroup sensitivities, a development window sensitivity analysis) and supersedes 2.x. The pipeline comprises: subject level and temporal development and deployment sets, DuckDB extraction with dictionary verified item identifiers, three frozen arms with Platt calibration and validation thresholds, a composite reward in [0, 1], fixed confidence action elimination with Hoeffding and empirical Bernstein anytime bounds, Thompson sampling, UCB1 and static, ensemble and heuristic comparators, a delayed feedback queue with a leakage assertion, 100 replicate simulation with paired bootstrap comparisons, sensitivity grids, an implied sample complexity table, a synthetic data mode, a unit test suite, continuous integration and a run manifest with MIMIC-IV file checksums. No patient level data are included; reproduction requires credentialed access to MIMIC-IV through PhysioNet.
